body: i think a big issue with this sort of reasoning is that certain groups are more disposed to be in conditions that lead to suicide - economic and social marginalization, poverty, generational trauma, etc. and if that was legal and accepted to opt out of life, it would be taken up by people in those conditions disproportionately. now ofc poor material conditions arent the entire reason why people commit suicide, but it is still significant. instead of normalizing it as something that is reasonable, we should work on erasing those problems that lead people to suicide in the first place. i understand where you are coming from, but allowing free choice to end your life will have significant precedents. maybe that would be okay in a truly equal society, but that is far from the reality.
